The left plot displays "Max" activation values on the y-axis against "Layer" number on the x-axis. The right plot displays "Final Value" on the y-axis against "Layer" number on the x-axis.

**Left Plot (Max vs. Layer):**
- **X-axis (Layer):** Labeled "Layer", it is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20. Tick marks are present at integer intervals (0, 5, 10, 15, 20), with no units specified.
- **Y-axis (Max):** Labeled "Max", it is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400. Tick marks are present at intervals of 100 (0, 100, 200, 300, 400), with no units specified.
- **Line 1 (Baseline - Red):** A red line with circular markers. It starts at approximately 0, rises sharply to a peak of 400 at layer 6, then drops to approximately 0 at layer 7. It remains near 0 until layer 15, then rises again to a peak of approximately 400 at layer 20.
- **Line 2 (SDPA Gating - Green):** A green line with circular markers. It starts at approximately 0, rises to a peak of approximately 200 at layer 6, then drops to approximately 0 at layer 7. It remains near 0 until layer 15, then rises again to a peak of approximately 200 at layer 20.
- **Line 3 (Value Layer Gating - Blue):** A blue line with circular markers. It starts at approximately 0, rises to a peak of approximately 200 at layer 6, then drops to approximately 0 at layer 7. It remains near 0 until layer 15, then rises again to a peak of approximately 200 at layer 20.
- **Line 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid - Orange):** An orange line with circular markers. It starts at approximately 0, rises to a peak of approximately 400 at layer 6, then drops to approximately 0 at layer 7. It remains near 0 until layer 15, then rises again to a peak of approximately 400 at layer 20.

**Right Plot (Final Value vs. Layer):**
- **X-axis (Layer):** Labeled "Layer", it is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20. Tick marks are present at integer intervals (0, 5, 10, 15, 20), with no units specified.
- **Y-axis (Final Value):** Labeled "Final Value", it is a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 2.0. Tick marks are present at intervals of 0.5 (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0), with no units specified.
- **Line 1 (Baseline - Red):** A red line with circular markers. It starts at 0.0, rises to 2.0 at layer 6, then drops to 0.0 at layer 7. It remains at 0.0 until layer 15, then rises again to 2.0 at layer 20.
- **Line 2 (SDPA Gating - Green):** A green line with circular markers. It starts at 0.0, rises to 1.0 at layer 6, then drops to 0.0 at layer 7. It remains at 0.0 until layer 15, then rises again to 1.0 at layer 20.
- **Line 3 (Value Layer Gating - Blue):** A blue line with circular markers. It starts at 0.0, rises to 1.0 at layer 6, then drops to 0.0 at layer 7. It remains at 0.0 until layer 15, then rises again to 1.0 at layer 20.
- **Line 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid - Orange):** An orange line with circular markers. It starts at 0.0, rises to 2.0 at layer 6, then drops to 0.0 at layer 7. It remains at 0.0 until layer 15, then rises again to 2.0 at layer 20.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations, displayed as two subplots. The left subplot plots "Max" activation values on the y-axis against "Layer" number on the x-axis, ranging from 0 to 20 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 5. The right subplot plots "Final Value" on the y-axis against "Layer" number on the x-axis, also ranging from 0 to 20 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 5. Row 1 (Baseline) shows a red line with a solid style and triangular markers, exhibiting a sharp increase to a peak of approximately 400 at layer 6, followed by a dip and then a steep rise to a peak of approximately 400 at layer 20. Row 2 (SDPA Gating) shows a green line with a solid style and triangular markers, remaining at a low value near 0 across all layers, with a slight upward trend near layer 20. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) shows a blue line with a solid style and triangular markers, showing a similar pattern to Row 2, remaining at a low value near 0 across all layers. Rows 4-5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) show a purple line with a solid style and triangular markers, exhibiting a pattern similar to Row 1, with a sharp increase to a peak of approximately 400 at layer 6, followed by a dip and then a steep rise to a peak of approximately 400 at layer 20.
model_annotations.English: Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network architecture. The plot is divided into five rows, each representing a distinct gating configuration: Row 1 (Baseline), Row 2 (SDPA Gating), Row 3 (Value Layer Gating), and Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid). Each row contains two subplots: the left subplot displays the mean activation magnitude (y-axis: “Mean”) across layers (x-axis: “Layer”, ranging from 0 to 20 with tick marks at integer intervals), while the right subplot shows the fraction of tokens (y-axis: “frac. tokens”) that are activated (ranging from 0.0 to 0.2) across layers (x-axis: “layer”, ranging from 0 to 20 with tick marks at integer intervals). In Row 1 (Baseline), the left plot shows a sharp rise in mean activation starting around layer 6, peaking near layer 10 at approximately 400, then declining slightly before rising again near layer 20. The right plot shows a corresponding rise in fraction of tokens activated starting around layer 6, reaching a peak near layer 10 at approximately 0.2, then declining slightly before rising again near layer 20. In Row 2 (SDPA Gating), the left plot shows a much lower mean activation magnitude, remaining below 100 across all layers with no significant peaks or declines. The right plot shows a similar trend, with the fraction of tokens activated remaining below 0.05 across all layers. In Row 3 (Value Layer Gating), the left plot shows a mean activation magnitude similar to Row 2, remaining below 100 across all layers with no significant peaks or declines. The right plot shows a similar trend, with the fraction of tokens activated remaining below 0.05 across all layers. In Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid), the left plot shows a mean activation magnitude similar to Row 1, with a sharp rise starting around layer 6, peaking near layer 10 at approximately 400, then declining slightly before rising again near layer 20. The right plot shows a similar trend, with the fraction of tokens activated rising starting around layer 6, reaching a peak near layer 10 at approximately 0.2, then declining slightly before rising again near layer 20.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm vergleicht die Verteilung von „Massive Activations“ und „Attention Sink“-Phänomenen über verschiedene Schichten (Layer) in einem neuronalen Netzwerk unter unterschiedlichen Gating-Konfigurationen. Die x-Achse ist mit „Layer“ beschriftet und zeigt einen linearen Skalenbereich von 0 bis 20, wobei die Tick-Markierungen in Einheiten von 5 angeordnet sind. Die y-Achse ist mit „Max“ beschriftet und verläuft linear von 0 bis 400, mit Tick-Markierungen in Einheiten von 100. In der ersten Reihe (Baseline) ist eine durchgezogene rote Linie zu sehen, die ab etwa Layer 6 einen starken Anstieg auf etwa 400 erreicht und danach abfällt, wobei ein deutlicher „Sink“-Effekt bei Layer 20 auftritt. In der zweiten Reihe (SDPA Gating) ist eine durchgezogene grüne Linie dargestellt, die eine deutlich reduzierte Aktivierung aufwies, ohne signifikante „Sink“-Phänomene. In der dritten Reihe (Value Layer Gating) zeigt eine durchgezogene blaue Linie ähnliche Aktivierungsverläufe wie die zweite Reihe, jedoch mit einem geringfügigen, residualen „Sink“-Effekt. In den vierten und fünften Reihen (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) sind zwei durchgezogene Linien in Orange und Lila zu sehen, die ähnliche Aktivierungsverläufe wie die erste Reihe aufweisen, einschließlich der starken Aktivierungen ab Layer 6 und des „Sink“-Effekts bei Layer 20.
